primitives.name: Projection-Based Lineup Generator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Vision The reference DFS lineup optimizer: a Python library that turns player pools + rule sets into valid DraftKings/FanDuel lineups, thousands at a time, with exposure control, stacking, and CSV import/export for bulk entry.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'player set, dimensionless', 'R': 'rule set, dimensionless', 'L': 'lineup, dimensionless', 'C': 'cost constraint, USD', 'V': 'value function, points'}
primitives.assumptions: Players are characterized by fixed cost and projection; optimization is deterministic and greedy.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When rule sets are inconsistent or player pool is empty.

layer2.mapping: GSE's lineup generation mirrors draftfast’s structure, but operates on live slates and external projections rather than precomputed inputs.
layer2.telemetry: Number of valid lineups generated per second, adherence to salary cap

primitives.name: Rule Set Data Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Covers NFL classic, Showdown, MVP; plus NBA/MLB/NHL/PGA/NASCAR/soccer/F1 and 20+ rule sets.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'sport type, categorical', 'T': 'contest type, categorical', 'M': 'max players per team, dimensionless', 'F': 'flexible positions, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Each sport has discrete rule configurations; rules are static during a contest period.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When new contests introduce novel constraints not present in existing rule sets.

layer2.mapping: GSE encodes rule sets as structured data, enabling dynamic composition of lineup constraints based on real-time contest parameters.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of rule application against official contest guidelines

primitives.name: Input Composition Layer
primitives.verbatim_quote: Input is a player pool with salary + projections (`Player(name, cost, proj, pos)` or a CSV from the contest's salaries export).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_i': 'player i, dimensionless', 'c_i': 'salary of player i, USD', 'p_i': 'projection of player i, points', 'pos_i': 'position of player i, categorical'}
primitives.assumptions: Player attributes are known and immutable within a given optimization window.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When input data is malformed or missing.

layer2.mapping: GSE treats input composition similarly, but sources player data from live feeds instead of static files.
layer2.telemetry: Data integrity check pass rate, latency of input ingestion

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight from draftfast is that the optimization process can be cleanly separated into three components: input data (players with cost/projection), rule sets defining valid lineups, and an optimizer that combines these. This modularization enables scalable, high-throughput lineup generation. However, draftfast's deterministic greedy approach lacks stochastic modeling of ownership or correlation effects, which limits its utility in GPPs. The failure mode occurs when rule sets are outdated or misapplied. In GSE, this translates to needing robust rule re-encoding and real-time validation. The architecture supports compositional reasoning over sports-specific constraints, allowing GSE to dynamically adapt to changing contest formats without hardcoding behavior.
